transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-21
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 8 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Sarah Patel (Head Eng - Lattice Credit), Miguel Ramos (CISO), Jenna Clarke (PM)

Auto-Summary:
- Discovery focused on data residency constraints, keystore residency, log minimization and geofence/fallback routing. Customer leaning towards Redwood Dedicated or Private for regulatory evidence; exploring Hosted with strict routing if possible.
- Main blockers: KMS residency, audit trail details, log redaction pipeline, and SLA for regional failover.

Topics:
- Residency zones (EU/UK/US regional splits)
- KMS/HSM key control and escrow options
- Log retention, pseudonymization and proof-of-deletion
- Network egress, VPC peering, and support for private control plane
- Trade-offs: latency/cost vs dedicated/private setup

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: alright hey everyone thanks for joining we're, um, Maya from Redwood, AE on this account - appreciate the time
[00:05] Sarah Patel: thanks Maya, yeah we wanted to dig into residency specifically — like where our traffic and keys live, and what evidence we can show to auditors
[00:12] Miguel Ramos: and also log minimization. we can't send full PII to external services, or at least we need proof we redacted before it leaves. so thats kind of the big ask
[00:25] Liam O'Neill: yup, totally. quick high level: Redwood supports three hosting modes — Hosted API (our standard), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for you), and Private (VPC / on-prem). For residency we can do region locking per tenant in Dedicated and Private, hosted can be region-restricted but keys and some metadata may still be in our control plane unless you use Private
[00:47] Jenna Clarke: can you clarify "control plane" — like does that include auth logs and user metadata? we need both to stay in the EU
[00:54] Liam O'Neill: good question. our hosted control plane currently runs in multi-region, and meta logs for provisioning are in the control plane. for EU residency customers we often recommend Dedicated with private control plane option or Private deployment so both data plane and control plane are under your VPC
[01:10] Sarah Patel: okay that's more clear. what about keys - we need KMS in-country with HSM backed keys, and ideally customer-managed keys
[01:18] Maya Chen: yep we support customer KMS integrations. For Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS (customer managed keys) or use an HSM provider; Private gives you full bring-your-own-keystore with HSM in your network
[01:28] Miguel Ramos: do you provide key escrow? legal requires ability to hand over key material in certain circumstances — or do we need a separate escrow product
[01:35] Liam O'Neill: we don't act as long term escrow by default; we can design a key routing strategy and documentation for escrow flows. for high security customers there is an enterprise add-on — we can loop legal/solutions on that
[01:48] Sarah Patel: log retention now — we want to retain minimal logs for 30 days, then archive only redacted aggregates. can Redwood support per-tenant retention policies and automatic redaction before logs leave the data plane
[02:02] Liam O'Neill: yes, per-tenant retention is supported in Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports retention controls but redaction is trickier since some telemetry hits our central pipeline. we have FIFO hooks for in-network redaction and a log-sanitization pipeline customer-side for Private
[02:18] Miguel Ramos: hmm so hosted is probably hard for us. are there hybrid options — run model in EU hosted but control plane in our VPC or vice versa
[02:26] Maya Chen: we do a couple hybrid patterns — most common is Hosted model endpoints in regional loci and a private control plane via VPC peering so sensitive metadata never crosses, but tokens may still route. it's a balance — we'll capture patterns in the doc we send
[02:39] Jenna Clarke: question on geofencing — during a region failure do you failover to another region? and how do you show that to auditors without breaking residency constraints
[02:48] Liam O'Neill: by default failover can go to secondary regions; for residency constrained customers we do region-locked policies with graceful rejection or fallback to a certified partner region. Some customers opt for automatic failover with data masking/pseudonymization before it moves
[03:05] Sarah Patel: can you do pseudonymization at source? i.e., from our app before sending to Redwood
[03:10] Liam O'Neill: yes that is a recommended pattern — strip PII client-side, send hashed identifiers and friendly tokens, then rehydrate in your control plane. we can provide an SDK snippet
[03:19] Miguel Ramos: audit evidence — we need signed tamper-evident logs, chain-of-custody. do you provide those artifacts for Dedicated or Private?
[03:28] Maya Chen: Dedicated and Private both give you full audit logs; Private gives you direct access to logs and we can enable signed log shipping to your SIEM. Dedicated can export signed bundles on request — we'll attach the SOC2/ISO excerpts
[03:40] Jenna Clarke: what about model caching and KV cache? could that leak data into long-lived cache across tenants
[03:46] Liam O'Neill: good callout. KV caches are per-deployment and per-tenant isolation is enforced at the runtime layer. we have guardrails that evict KV per session and TTLs; for high-security installs we can disable caching entirely
[03:58] Sarah Patel: curious about the cost and latency tradeoffs — Dedicated or Private looks more expensive, but maybe we need it for compliance
[04:05] Maya Chen: yes Dedicated gives predictability and isolation at moderate premium; Private has higher ops footprint but gives full control. We can run an initial perf baseline to estimate overheads vs hosted
[04:15] Miguel Ramos: ok can we talk about legal hold? in an e-discovery case we might need to hold data longer — how is that handled
[04:21] Liam O'Neill: we support legal hold workflows: flagged data is moved to immutable store under your retention settings. For Private you get direct control; for Dedicated we run the pipeline and can provide immutable snapshots
[04:31] Sarah Patel: are there specific certifications for the hardware side? our auditors ask about FIPS, HSMs
[04:36] Maya Chen: our HSM partners are FIPS 140-2/3 compliant; hardware attestation and chain of custody for HSM-backed keys is standard in the Private offering
[04:45] Jenna Clarke: what's the timeline to stand up a Dedicated environment for a pilot? we want to run an LLM-powered underwriting helper in EU region in 6 weeks
[04:54] Maya Chen: we can provision a small Dedicated pool in ~3-4 weeks for pilot (depends on quota and capacity); Private takes longer — typically 6-10 weeks with on-prem requirements
[05:05] Miguel Ramos: okay i'd like more detail on logs we would still see outside the region under Hosted — can you enumerate what metadata leaves our zone
[05:14] Liam O'Neill: generally provisioning events, billing metadata, anonymized telemetry for perf— may include model name and latency buckets but not raw prompt data; we'll produce a mapping table in the follow-up doc
[05:26] Sarah Patel: do you support SSO/SAML SCIM and RBAC integration with our IdP
[05:31] Maya Chen: yes SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning supported across offerings; RBAC can be enforced per-team/route
[05:38] Jenna Clarke: any limits to encryption in transit for private peering? like mTLS only or support for IPsec tunnels
[05:43] Liam O'Neill: we support mTLS and IPsec for Dedicated/Private peering; private control plane can use dedicated circuits if needed
[05:52] Miguel Ramos: one more — do you keep any raw prompts in logs for debugging? we can't allow that in EU
[05:57] Liam O'Neill: by default debug logs redact prompts; debug traces with prompt content are only generated with explicit customer opt-in and are stored in region if requested
[06:07] Sarah Patel: can you walk quickly through what evidence we'd get for SOC2 or ISO audit
[06:12] Maya Chen: sure — we'll include SOC2 report excerpt, control mappings (log access, key control), network diagrams, and sample signed log bundle. for Private we provide direct access to the evidence repository
[06:24] Jenna Clarke: awesome. let's talk about cost center mapping — we may want per-team billing and token caps
[06:30] Maya Chen: per-route and per-token billing and quotas are supported, with spend alerts
[06:36] Miguel Ramos: any concerns re: model updates - will we get a heads up before model or kernel creds change? need change control
[06:42] Liam O'Neill: we do version pinning and rollout policies. for Dedicated customers you can pin to a model binary and schedule updates; Private you control the updates completely
[06:51] Sarah Patel: got it. we'll compile our regulatory matrix and share a short list of required controls
[06:56] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll send the KMS note, SOC2 excerpts and the control mapping doc
[07:01] Jenna Clarke: do you have a small sample of the redaction pipeline we can review - like a code snippet
[07:06] Liam O'Neill: yes we'll include an SDK snippet and sample K8s sidecar pattern for pre-send redaction
[07:13] Maya Chen: cool, i think we're in good shape to follow up. any final items?
[07:17] Miguel Ramos: one ask: include a clear statement on whether any identifiers are ever replicated to central control plane under Hosted
[07:24] Maya Chen: noted - we'll add explicit table per field
[07:26] Sarah Patel: thanks everyone
[07:29] Maya Chen: thanks all. recap next steps - we'll shoot the doc and schedule the perf call
